pr.title: Micro-optimization attempt in coroutine layout computation

In `compute_layout`, there were a bunch of collections (`IndexVec`s) that were being created by `push`ing in a loop, instead of a, hopefully, more performant usage of iterator combinators. [Second commit](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/commit/6f682c2774c09840931a55bcf6691799ce21e5e1) is just a small cleanup.

I'd love a perf run to see if this shows up in benchmarks.
pr.author: yotamofek

processing.reason: The supplied PR is explicitly a performance/cleanup refactor of `compute_layout`, and the decoded head source shows the refactor is semantically equivalent to the push-based construction: `variant_fields` still has exactly `RESERVED_VARIANTS + live_locals_at_suspension_points.len()` entries, the `.skip(RESERVED_VARIANTS)` keeps suspension variants aligned, `*fields = live_locals.iter().collect()` preserves per-variant field order, `fields.iter_enumerated()` preserves the same `FieldIdx` values as the old `enumerate()` + `FieldIdx::from_usize`, and `variant_source_info` is extended with the same three reserved entries before pushing the same paired source infos. `izip!` does not truncate here because both suspension-point vectors are pushed together and `variant_fields` is pre-sized to their exact length. No source-grounded semantic bug or historical wrong-value assignment is present in the PR diff or head source; the only ways to force a difference would be to intentionally remove `.skip(...)`, misuse the suspension-point index as the field index, or otherwise invent a transformation not made by this PR. Therefore no valid original/transformed counterexample pair can be constructed without manufacturing an unrelated change.

evidence: In `compute_layout`, there were a bunch of collections (`IndexVec`s) that were being created by `push`ing in a loop, instead of a, hopefully, more performant usage of iterator combinators.
I'd love a perf run to see if this shows up in benchmarks.
Note that if a field is included in multiple variants, we will
// just use the first one here. That's fine; fields do not move
// around inside coroutines, so it doesn't matter which variant
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically proposed optimization changes representation/construction without changing intended layout: it preallocates `locals`/`tys` with `saved_locals.domain_size()`, preallocates `variant_source_info` with `CoroutineArgs::RESERVED_VARIANTS + live_locals_at_suspension_points.len()` and extends it with the three reserved infos, creates `variant_fields` via `IndexVec::from_elem_n(IndexVec::new(), CoroutineArgs::RESERVED_VARIANTS + live_locals_at_suspension_points.len())`, then uses `izip!` over `&live_locals_at_suspension_points`, `&source_info_at_suspension_points`, and `variant_fields.iter_enumerated_mut().skip(CoroutineArgs::RESERVED_VARIANTS)`. In each iteration it assigns `*fields = live_locals.iter().collect()` and iterates `fields.iter_enumerated()` so `idx` remains the per-variant `FieldIdx` used by `remap`, then pushes the paired source info. This is a merged optimization attempt; no compiler execution or reproduced defect is claimed.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust coroutine/async lowering functions processed by `StateTransform` in `compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/coroutine.rs`, specifically `locals_live_across_suspend_points` and `compute_layout`, with zero or more `TerminatorKind::Yield` suspension points, movable and immovable coroutines, borrowed locals crossing suspension points, and per-suspension-point live-local sets that may overlap across variants.
analysis.originalLogic: The original `compute_layout` built collections with repeated pushes: `variant_source_info` started from three reserved entries collected from an array of outermost SourceInfos; `variant_fields` started with `CoroutineArgs::RESERVED_VARIANTS` empty `IndexVec`s via `iter::repeat(IndexVec::new()).take(...)`; then for each suspension point it created `fields` and pushed saved locals with their enumerate index, converted via `FieldIdx::from_usize(idx)`, recorded `remap[locals[saved_local]] = Some((tys[saved_local].ty, variant_index, idx))`, pushed `fields` into `variant_fields`, and separately pushed the matching SourceInfo. Suspension-point variant indices were `VariantIdx::from(CoroutineArgs::RESERVED_VARIANTS + suspension_point_idx)`.
pitfalls: Dropping the `.skip(CoroutineArgs::RESERVED_VARIANTS)` and iterating `variant_fields` from index 0 would assign suspension-point fields into reserved variants and misalign variant indices.
Preallocating only `live_locals_at_suspension_points.len()` for `variant_fields` instead of adding `CoroutineArgs::RESERVED_VARIANTS` would lose or shift reserved variant slots.
Using the suspension-point index as the field index instead of the index within the current `fields` vector would corrupt `remap` whenever different variants have different live-local sets.
Changing `remap` insertion order or overwriting entries for duplicated saved locals could change which variant/field pair is selected, despite fields not moving within the coroutine.
Treating `izip!` as a length check is unsafe: unequal liveness, source-info, and variant-field iterators can silently omit trailing suspension points.
preconditions: Reserved coroutine variants (UNRESUMED/RETURNED/POISONED) must remain the first `CoroutineArgs::RESERVED_VARIANTS` entries in both `variant_source_info` and `variant_fields`.
`variant_fields` must have exactly one entry per reserved variant plus one per suspension point, in the same order used to derive each suspension point's `VariantIdx`.
`variant_source_info` and `variant_fields` must stay aligned with `live_locals_at_suspension_points`; `izip!` silently truncates if the iterators have different lengths.
Within each suspension-point variant, saved locals must be enumerated starting at field 0, because the stored `remap` entry uses that `FieldIdx` to address the field in the variant.
When a saved local appears in multiple variants, the first assignment to `remap` is intentionally retained: fields do not move between coroutine variants.
analysis.summary: In coroutine layout computation, replace loop-push construction of IndexVecs with pre-sized capacities, IndexVec::from_elem_n, and itertools::izip over suspension-point liveness, source info, and mutable variant-field slots. This is a performance/cleanup optimization, not a confirmed bug fix; its correctness depends on preserving reserved-variant offsets, variant ordering, and per-variant field indices.
analysis.testStrategy: Add or inspect MIR/layout tests for coroutines with at least two suspension points whose live saved-local sets differ, plus a case where the same saved local is live across multiple suspension points. Compare `CoroutineSavedLocal` to layout `(ty, VariantIdx, FieldIdx)` remapping, variant field lists, variant source-info ordering, and debug info against the push-based construction. Include immovable coroutines with borrowed locals to exercise the union/intersect liveness path. These are suggested compile-time MIR/layout comparisons only; no execution or reproduction was performed.
analysis.trigger: Optimizing coroutine layout bookkeeping when a coroutine has suspension points: collections indexed by `CoroutineSavedLocal`, `VariantIdx`, and `FieldIdx` are constructed while scanning `live_locals_at_suspension_points` and their paired `source_info_at_suspension_points`.
